title: Requirement file (YAML)
description: Structural contract for requirement YAML files under engine/requirements/. A file is a requirement *container*; its `description` map holds the numbered shall-statements, each an object carrying its own upward trace (`source` XOR `derived` for HLR, `parent_req` for LLR). The file's level is determined by its filename prefix: `hlr_` -> high-level (validate against $defs/hlr), `llr_` -> low-level (validate against $defs/llr). Cross-field and cross-file rules that JSON Schema cannot express (description-key contiguity, RS.2 ID uniqueness, parent_req referential integrity, the RS.3 one-shall lint) are enforced by src/reqs/checks/schema.py.

hlrStatement.$comment: One atomic shall-statement. Its trace is carried per-statement: exactly one of `source` / `derived` (oneOf: both-present yields two matches and fails; neither yields zero and fails -- an HLR statement that traces nowhere must be explicitly marked derived).

hlrDescriptionMap.$comment: Numbered, atomic shall-statements. YAML integer keys are stringified before schema validation; the validator separately enforces that keys are integers contiguous from 1.

llrStatement.$comment: One atomic shall-statement. Its trace is carried per-statement in `parent_req`.

llrDescriptionMap.$comment: Numbered, atomic shall-statements. YAML integer keys are stringified before schema validation; the validator separately enforces that keys are integers contiguous from 1.

visibility.$comment: Audience/exposure of the implemented entity. The vocabulary is project-defined; the schema fixes only the slot's shape (a non-empty string), not its value set. Runtime examples use compiler/api/internal.
